newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine health plan hit by 24-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Argentine health plan hit by 24-hour strike.

text.p: Argentina's huge state-run pensioners' health system PAMI faced a 24-hour strike Monday by contracted clinics and doctors over months of unpaid bills.
About 40,000 doctors all over the country joined the strike, attending only emergency cases and in-patients.

Norberto Larroca, head of the Argentine Confederation of Clinics, Sanatoriums and Private Hospitals, told local radio his members were "on the brink of bankruptcy" because they had not been paid the $21 or $22 they charge per pensioner.
"They owe us four months of $22 pesos, which nationwide adds up to about $300 million, while current services are being paid only from time to time," said Larroca.
Argentine President Carlos Menem last week gave the PAMI three months to sort out its problems -- including the $1.2 billion debt run up in just two years.

But while the private clinics and doctors that tend to PAMI members complained the debts were taking them to the brink of collapse, PAMI administrator Alejandro Bramer Markovic alleged overcharging and political manipulation of the PAMI, which has an annual budget of nearly $2.5 billion.
"The PAMI has been manipulated by everyone, including by contractors, who charge very high prices for their services," he told Clarin newspaper in an interview published Monday.

"The PAMI has been managed on political criteria and not with business criteria. Now it will cease to be a political bounty," said Bramer Markovic, appointed by Menem to reform an organism which is constantly accused of corruption.
He said that the 300 internal audits he had ordered and an audit by the National General Auditor had turned up "serious anomalies and waste."

The PAMI administrator said his aim was to "stop this hemorrhage of funds, by offering better services at a lower price, with a change in the system to let each beneficiary choose freely the most suitable service."
